## One fabric for two worlds

You explain the elegant architecture of <span id="ch1.intro1.2"/>: by using advanced open-source technologies on a **<span id="assignment.2.2"/> foundation**, the platform does not just *tolerate* virtual machines: it treats them as **native citizens of the container ecosystem**. The heavy virtual machines will run side-by-side with the nimble containers, managed by the exact same orchestration engine:

| Virtualization world | <span id="assignment.14.1"/> World | Unified on <span id="ch1.intro1.2"/> |
|---------------------|----------------|-------------------------------|
| Hypervisor hosts | <span id="assignment.2.2"/> nodes | **One set of nodes runs both** |
| Hypervisor management console | Container tooling | **One platform underneath**. <span id="ch1.intro1.2"/> runs the VMs, Rancher Prime commands the clusters and the containers |
| SAN storage arrays | <span id="assignment.2.9"/> volumes | **<span id="assignment.2.8"/> serves VMs and pods alike** |

That last row is where you start. Every VM disk, every container's persistent volume, all of it rides on the same distributed storage fabric, and not every workload deserves the same price tag.



## 🎯 Your Quest Objectives

1. Inspect the physical node topology
2. Prepare a dedicated workspace
3. Understand how <span id="assignment.2.8"/> replicates your data
4. Build a cost-tier storage class for the development team



🔐 Login Credentials
====================
